answer.rationale: The write-path p99 climbing to 5x target within 90 minutes, coinciding with a release 2 hours ago, is a strong temporal-correlation signal. Memory b1 (day 18) records that rolling back a release cleared a checkout error spike cleanly with no customer impact; I want the archived source to confirm the rollback mechanism and that the prior build was genuinely stable before I commit. Memory b3 (day 47) documents that provisioning headroom absorbed a surge without queue-depth growth; I want the source to confirm whether the headroom play is viable under simultaneous heavy settlement traffic. If the rollback source confirms the prior build's stability and a clean cutover path, rollback_release is the single highest-leverage intervention: it directly removes the most likely cause of the latency regression, preserves all customer writes (no traffic is shed), and avoids the risk of adding capacity into a code-path regression or failing over while the defective build is still live. Regional failover and circuit breakers address topology or dependency failures, not a suspected bad release. Routing to read replicas does not help a write-path problem. Add capacity treats a symptom that is almost certainly caused by the release and would waste the single intervention window.
